The change that fixed this is commit `c21a7cbf` ("TRUNK-6683: Skip full-text search with drugs when a concept is provided (#6346)", by Ian). It adds `concept == null` to the condition that guards the ConceptName full-text lookup in `HibernateConceptDAO.newDrugQuery`. When a concept is supplied, the lookup is skipped and the drug query runs on the drug/concept fields only. Falkon lists the commit under the repository name `github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core`, and the PR number comes from the commit title.

The fix is in `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateConceptDAO.java`, at lines 1582–1583. The new comment reads "If a concept is supplied, skip the relatively expensive concept-name full-text search". Before the change, the guard was only `if (searchDrugConceptNames)`. The concept-name `SearchQueryUnique.findUniqueKeys` call (lines 1584–1590) therefore ran even when a concept was given. Its result only added boosted `concept.conceptId` clauses, so with a concept supplied it was redundant with the existing `concept.conceptId` boost at line 1601.

The service layer just delegates. `ConceptServiceImpl.getDrugs(...)` at lines 1579–1581 calls `dao.getDrugs(...)` with no logic of its own, so the change is entirely in the DAO. The commit also adds two tests in `HibernateConceptDAOTest` (one that checks the lookup is skipped when a concept is supplied, one that checks it still runs without a concept) and a fixture concept/drug in `HibernateConceptTestDataSet.xml`.

I didn't run the test suite; the evidence above comes from reading the commit diff and the current source.
